summary: ETraining is a web page used to redirect authenticated users to an external Moodle training portal. It ensures users are logged in, prepares credentials invisibly, and adapts for French Canadian users. If the user session is invalid, they are redirected to a timeout page.
purpose: To facilitate secure, seamless login and redirection from HSPnet to a Moodle eTraining portal, passing session and credential information through a hidden form.

fields.name: form1
fields.description: Main redirect form. Posts to Moodle URL.

fields.name: Submit
fields.description: Button to submit form, labeled with training access resource.

workflows.name: Redirect to Moodle Training
steps: Page loads and checks if UserSession.SessionID > 0.
If valid, sets form1.Action to MoodleTrainingURL/login/index.php.
If UserSession.Locale == 'fr-CA', appends ?lang=fr_ca to Action for French login.
Sets username value to ProvinceCode + UserID.
Sets Submit button label to localized training access string.
Form is presented and ready for submission.
If user submits, form posts credentials to Moodle in a new window.
If session is invalid, redirects user to Timedout.aspx with session query string.

business_rules: Only users with valid UserSession.SessionID (> 0) can access eTraining.
French Canadian users are redirected with language set to fr_ca.
User credentials are securely passed as hidden form fields.
Invalid sessions trigger a timeout redirect.
validations: SessionID must be present and greater than zero.
Locale must be checked for French Canadian.
conditions: If UserSession.SessionID > 0: proceed to Moodle redirect.
If Locale == 'fr-CA': add lang=fr_ca to Action URL.
system_behavior: Prepares form fields invisibly for user.
Forms are submitted in a new browser window (target='_blank').
exceptions: If SessionID is invalid (<=0), redirects to timeout page.
content_gaps: No explicit detail about Moodle endpoint requirements.
Unclear if additional user attributes are required for training access.
Error handling for failed form submission is not described.
